payload.title: fix 4 real gaps in knowledge registry lifecycle enforcement found in code review (follow-on from…
payload.description: fix 4 real gaps in knowledge registry lifecycle enforcement found in code review (follow-on from tsk-28x's fix(knowledge) series): (1) P1: doc.register (src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs ~L420, ~L444) bypasses the lifecycle state machine -- it lets a re-register of an existing docId overwrite docLifecycle freely, so re-running register without --lifecycle can silently demote active back to provisional, and can resurrect a retired/superseded doc back to active, breaking doc.promote as the sole provisional->active gate. Fix: doc.register on an existing docId must preserve current lifecycle and reject any lifecycle transition it's given, not just check the (topicId, role) slot via assertDocSlotAvailable. (2) P1: attest is still possible against a superseded doc -- src/report/knowledge-resolver.mjs:24 only excludes retired docs from resolution, and the reducer at src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs:551 only rejects attest into retired, not superseded. So knowledge attest --doc-path <old-current-path> still resolves and writes a capture linkage onto a doc that is no longer authoritative. Fix: exclude superseded (not just retired) from the live resolver, and reject doc.attest into a superseded doc in the reducer. (3) P1: topic.merge (src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs:291) only checks that targetTopicId exists, not that it's active -- merging into a retired topic locks out all new writes afterward. topic.split (src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs:221) only checks source exists, not active -- splitting an already-retired topic creates a new active successor out of an ended lineage. Fix: require source of split and target of merge to have status === 'active', with regression tests. (4) P2: topic.retire (src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs:365) on a nonexistent topicId is a silent no-op instead of throwing -- CLI reports success with no actual state change. Fix: fail-closed like doc.retire/doc.supersede already do. Context: docs/architect/knowledge-registry-redesign.md is the design doc; there is already uncommitted WIP on main (src/state/knowledge-registry.mjs, bin/fgos.mjs, src/cli/command-registry.mjs, scripts/knowledge-canary.mjs + their tests) implementing the two items this same review already found closed (--capture-id required + attest rejects retired doc/topic) -- that WIP should move into this item's worktree and continue from there, not be redone.

payload.text: Landed fgw/tsk-3uc into main manually (commit 36433e5), bypassing fgos approve
payload.rationale: fgos approve's own merge/move state machine hit a reproducible internal bug under repeated retry: a durably-written awaiting-approval work.move event (seq 16) vanished from the event log within seconds of being confirmed present, then the next approve call crashed with 'transitionWork: expected awaiting-approval ... found blocked' (exit 3) instead of a clean structured block response. Reproduced 3 times with fresh fgos list confirmation each time; user confirmed no other session/agent was touching this item. User explicitly chose (after being shown the evidence and 3 options) to bypass fgos approve: manually ran git merge --no-commit --no-ff fgw/tsk-3uc on the main checkout, resolved all conflicts (a real CHANGELOG.md content conflict already fixed earlier in fgw/tsk-3uc itself via commit c113c87, plus .fgos/ path noise -- config.json conflict, several modify/delete conflicts, and 2 files where git's line-merge picked the branch's shorter historical content over main's current content -- all resolved by keeping main's own current .fgos/ state per ADR0020), ran full npm test (4238 tests, 4233 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped), then committed the merge (36433e5). No path under .fgos/ differs from main's pre-merge HEAD. This tool bug will be reported separately via feedback.

payload.title: Bug in fgos approve/move state machine: a durably-written work.move event vanishes from the event…
payload.description: Bug in fgos approve/move state machine: a durably-written work.move event vanishes from the event log within ~1 minute, then the next fgos approve call crashes with a raw CAS error instead of a clean block. Repro: get an item stuck in a merge-failed-unclassified block caused by live .fgos/ event-log dirt on the main checkout (easy to trigger since fgOS's own CLI calls constantly append to .fgos/events/<writer>-*.jsonl on the main checkout, and approve's git merge --no-commit --no-ff refuses outright on any dirty tracked path under .fgos/). Then loop `fgos move <id> --to awaiting-approval --expect blocked` followed immediately by `fgos approve <id> --acknowledge-iron-law` a few times in quick succession. Observed on item tsk-3uc (forgentX repo): fgos move returned success JSON with a seq that was NOT actually written durably in two calls (confirmed via direct grep of .fgos/events/*.jsonl raw files, not fgos list, which itself appeared to show the moved status even when the underlying event never landed). On a later call a real event DID land (seq 16, work.move to awaiting-approval, confirmed present in the raw log via grep immediately after). Within about a minute, after fgos approve failed again with the same recurring merge-failed-unclassified reason, that same seq-16 event had disappeared entirely from the raw event log (rechecked twice, gone both times, not present in any .fgos/events/archive/ or baseline-*.jsonl file either). The very next fgos approve call then crashed with the message `fgos: transitionWork: expected status "awaiting-approval" for work "tsk-3uc" but found "blocked" — refusing to overwrite blindly` and exit code 3 -- this is a raw uncaught-looking error, not the normal structured {to:"blocked", reason:...} JSON envelope approve produces for every other classified block reason (merge-conflict, verify-fail-post-merge, etc). No other session or agent was touching this item (explicitly confirmed with the user before the final repro). Suspected but NOT verified root cause: approve's own internal retry/cleanup path on a second consecutive merge failure may perform a git-level reset/checkout under .fgos/ that discards a just-appended live event before its own second internal precondition re-check runs, producing the CAS mismatch -- needs real source-level investigation in src/runner/merge.mjs (mergeRunnerItemLocked area) and src/state/store.mjs (transitionWork). Impact: approve/move become unusable for an item stuck in repeated merge-failed-unclassified blocks -- forces a manual git-merge bypass of the whole approve verb to land the item, skipping approve's blast-radius display, verify re-run, and proper mergedSha/mergedInto metadata recording. Evidence: forgentX repo, item id tsk-3uc, event-log seq 12-17 in .fgos/events/f9ffb383-f6a6-4b9c-b9c6-e3a1cc338244-*.jsonl, decision log entries on tsk-3uc at 2026-08-27T03:00:44Z and 2026-08-27T03:21:21Z narrate the full timeline. Workaround used: manual git merge --no-commit --no-ff, manual .fgos/ conflict resolution keeping main's own current content per ADR0020, full npm test (4238 pass), manual commit (36433e5), then fgos move --to delivered directly, each move step verified against the raw event log rather than trusting the CLI's JSON response.
